idiom_name: final class kit over a [String: () -> Product] dictionary of closures
implementation_notes: A Swift kit is a Dictionary keyed by String (or by ObjectIdentifier / Any.Type when the key should be a type) whose values are closures, wrapped in a final class so the registry can be mutated through a reference, with a throwing create(_:) that names the missing key instead of returning an optional. What replaces the classic structure: the dictionary and the closures - subclass factories are unnecessary, and value semantics are why the kit must be a reference type if it is to be filled after construction. Framework precedent: Foundation's ValueTransformer keeps registered instances under names via setValueTransformer(_:forName:) for later lookup by the binding runtime, the same name-to-implementation registry at framework scale. Reflective construction (Bundle.classNamed, NSClassFromString) is the fallback when a key must resolve to a class rather than to a closure.
pitfalls: The dictionary retains its closures, so a singleton kit keeps every captured dependency alive for the process lifetime - the classic listener/leak symptom in Swift.
Dictionary is a value type: store it in a var on a class (or make the kit a class) or registrations made through one copy are invisible to another.
Bundle.classNamed / NSClassFromString need the module-qualified name and are unavailable outside Apple platforms, so keep reflection for dynamic plugin names and closures for everything else.
